frequency_question: What proportion of major high-profile partisan voting or election integrity bills that achieve floor consideration or chamber movement successfully pass their originating or target chamber with exact textual requirements before the deadline?
membership_rule: Includes major federal election-related bills that explicitly require documentary proof of citizenship or major procedural voting changes; excludes non-voting general bills or riders that did not receive standalone chamber votes.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act Amendments (various partisan attempts)
Help America Vote Act (HAVA) partisan provisions

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.7x)
coverage_note: 10 major legislative attempts identified across three decades of polarized election legislation; 4 successfully cleared targeted chamber thresholds meeting specific structural definitions.
known_gaps: Excludes minor committee-only bills that never reached chamber-wide votes.
skeleton: Total notable partisan federal election integrity or access bills introduced and pushed to chamber consideration since 1994, decomposed by whether exact criteria including naming provisions or identical successor clauses were met within the session limit.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 10 major legislative pushes meeting the procedural framing structure = 40% base satisfaction rate given substantive movement.
validity_reason: Valid through the current congressional cycle structure until structural polarization dynamics or chamber rules shift significantly.
